description: Pick a chart type from the question being asked and the shape of the data. Pass `question` (compare, trend, distribution, part-to-whole, relationship, ranking, geography) and any of: `categories` (number of groups or items), `points` (observations or time steps), `series` (number of series), `thirdVariable` (relationship questions: a third measure to encode), `hierarchy` (parts nest inside parts), `overTime` (the question is across time), `audience` (general or analyst). Returns `ranked` chart types, each with a reason tied to your numbers, `avoid` (chart types that mislead for this question) and `notes`. Draws on the practice described by Stephen Few (Show Me the Numbers) and Alberto Cairo (The Functional Art); the rankings are our own judgement, not a formula. Pure computation.

points.description: Number of observations or time points.

question.description: What the reader should be able to answer.
